capture_method: Native complete R4 model; exact AnimationPlayer seek; two complete renders to settle GPU skin upload; four shared-world camera views. Every clip start/end also compares a third draw pixel-for-pixel.
scope: Actual visual examination of each image row and all four views; quantitative mesh/collision distances are validated in separate native and Blender reports.
caveats: These body atlases have 384 by 448 pixels per direction; submillimeter surface distances and intersections are assessed by the separate mesh/fabric probes.

The isolated ladder atlases omit ladder geometry and apply the declared 0.30 m/s upward root travel. Physical rung contact, traversal exit and actual collapse are assessed in the native runtime/demo reports and final live ladder captures.

atlases.observation: The guarded stance begins a gradual knee and hip compression. Both boots stay planted, elbows hold distinct rigid arm segments, and shirt sleeves, waist hem and trouser silhouettes remain continuous in all four views.

Crouch anticipation deepens progressively with forward torso inclination and slightly drawing-in hands. Foot placement is stable; wrists maintain claw shapes without stretching; no visible cloth inversion or sudden shoulder-volume change.

The knees and hips compress into the lower anticipation pose while hands remain guarded in front. Side views show a readable squat with no arm-length distortion. Sleeve edges, trouser knees and rear shirt panels stay continuous.

The bottom of the crouch transitions into leg extension and initial lift around the takeoff marker. The feet maintain their stance width, shoulders retain volume, and there is no visible pop or garment spike between consecutive rows.

The zombie rises visibly off the floor while reaching its guarded hands forward. Elbows remain bent and anatomically distinct, boots lift together, and shoulder, sleeve, waist and trouser volumes remain consistent.

The shallow jump apex is clear in all directions with both soles above the floor. The restrained arm guard stays stable while the body changes height; no noodle-like stretch, shirt flash or knee-volume collapse is visible.

The body descends smoothly from the apex and hands draw back toward the guard. Knee and elbow proportions remain stable, with no visible sleeve collapse, waist gap or frame-to-frame pose discontinuity.

Landing develops into a clear impact-absorption crouch around the authored landing phase. The knees and hips bend while both boots settle at the floor, and the torso and hands recover together without distorted limb lengths or inverted cloth silhouettes.

The deepest landing crouch eases into recovery. Bent knees keep their cloth volume, hands remain in a controlled guard, and the shirt hem and sleeve openings retain a stable silhouette through the lowest frames.
Legs extend gradually out of the landing crouch while the feet hold position. Front and rear views retain shoulder width and arm proportions; no sudden cloth jump or detached-looking cuff is visible.
Recovery settles smoothly toward the initial guarded stance. Arm lengths and elbow shape remain unchanged, both boots stay planted, and shoulder, waist and knee fabric remain coherent.
The final settling frames hold a deliberate guarded recovery pose with only small eased movement. No snap, stretched wrist or garment discontinuity appears approaching the endpoint.

The final endpoint returns to the original guarded stance cleanly, with matching limb proportions and continuous shirt, trousers and boots. No last-frame snap is visible against the preceding recovery rows.

The climb opens in an asymmetric support pose with one knee high and one hand reaching above the head. Elbows remain distinct, the lifted knee retains trouser volume, and the sleeves and upper-back cloth remain continuous. These isolated body views do not include physical ladder rungs.

The torso rises through the held support phase as the lower leg begins changing position. The raised hand keeps a firm curved grip shape and both forearms retain their lengths. Shirt shoulders, waist and lifted-knee cloth stay coherent.

Weight shifts toward the next step: the lower knee starts lifting and the previously raised knee extends relative to the rising torso. All four views retain clear knee and elbow geometry without an abrupt hand or shoulder pop.

The knees pass through the mid-step configuration while the body rises; the hands maintain their support/reach relationship. Forearms stay rigid and the compressed knee, hip and back-shirt areas show no visible collapse or inversion.

The opposite knee gains height as the lower hand starts its next reach. Arm and leg segments remain proportional, shoulders rotate without collapsing sleeve volume, and the waist and trouser silhouettes remain continuous.

Both hands pass near head height during the grip exchange, then the next reaching hand lifts. Front and back views retain lateral clearance around the face, while side views show a clear elbow hinge. No visible sleeve inversion or knee-cloth spike appears.

The new reaching arm rises as the opposite arm holds support and the knees alternate height. The raised elbow and upper arm keep their volume, wrist curvature stays localized to the hand, and trouser folds remain continuous through the deeper bend.

The reaching arm extends to its higher support pose while the opposite knee stays lifted. The shoulder and sleeve retain a rounded volume, the forearm stays proportional, and waist and knee folds do not visibly flip or spike.

The higher hand and opposing support hand settle into the next hold as the torso continues rising. The deep knee bend preserves trouser thickness, the back-shirt surface remains coherent, and frame 53 is consistent with the separately rendered live ladder-release starting pose.

The half-cycle support pose holds while the body ascends, with one high hand and one high knee. Forearm and shin lengths stay fixed, the lower hand remains controlled, and no visible shirt or trouser fold inversion occurs.
The second half-cycle begins with the opposite-side support pattern. The lower foot starts preparing the next step, and shoulder, elbow, knee and waist silhouettes stay continuous as the torso rises.

The lower knee lifts into the second step while the previous support leg extends relative to the torso. The upper hand holds a stable grip shape, and elbows, sleeves and trouser knees retain consistent thickness.

The body passes through the second mid-step crouch, with both knees bent before the next exchange. Arm and torso proportions remain coherent in all four views, and the waist and underarm fabric show no visible tearing or sudden fold reversal.

The support legs pass through the middle of their exchange while the hands retain staggered heights. Clear elbow bends and a stable shoulder silhouette remain visible; knee and seat fabric preserve their volume.

The next reaching hand begins rising while the new knee takes height. The opposite hand remains controlled near the support position. No obvious cloth inversion, stretched forearm or discontinuous wrist movement appears across the six frames.

The second grip exchange passes both hands near head height with maintained lateral spacing. Shoulder width and elbow volumes remain stable; the bent knee and trouser seat retain a readable solid silhouette.

The next reaching arm rises toward the original-side high support while the legs continue alternating. Forearms remain firm segments, finger curvature stays confined to the hands, and the sleeves and waist remain visually continuous.

The reaching arm approaches its higher grip and the newly raised knee stabilizes. Upper-arm and forearm sections remain distinct, elbow curvature is controlled, and the sleeve and upper-back surfaces retain volume.

The support pattern returns toward the cycle's opening configuration while the root continues upward. Deep knee cloth and the raised shoulder stay coherent; no sudden pose or fabric discontinuity is visible as the loop endpoint approaches.

The loop settles toward its opening asymmetric hand-and-knee support pose. Shoulder and knee volumes remain stable, hand curvature stays controlled, and no endpoint approach pop or garment flash appears.

The final endpoint matches the opening body configuration after the declared upward root travel. The arm proportions, sleeve openings, trouser knees and boots remain coherent, and the support pattern closes without a visible pose snap.

summary: All 73 jump poses and 121 ladder poses were actually inspected in four views, including each 60 Hz frame and both endpoints.
The jump has readable crouch anticipation, shallow flight, landing compression and guarded recovery. Arm segment proportions and garment silhouettes remain visually stable.
The ladder cycle alternates reaching hands and lifted knees while the root rises. Shoulder, elbow and knee volumes remain coherent and the support pose closes smoothly at the loop endpoint.
